{{Quote|Execute Order 66.|[[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] to numerous clone commanders|audio=ExecuteOrder66.flac|<ref name="RotS">{{Film|III}}</ref>}}
'''Order 66''', also known as '''Clone Protocol 66''' or '''Protocol 66''', was one of the series of [[Contingency Orders for the Grand Army of the Republic: Order Initiation, Orders 1 Through 150|contingency orders]] that the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]] of the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] were required to obey without question. The order was programmed into the Clone Troopers through an [[Inhibitor chip/Legends|inhibitor chip]] to ensure that the Clones would obey the command. The order branded members of the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] as traitors to the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] and called for their immediate execution without question. The issuing of the order by [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] caused clone troopers to obey it immediately, due to the programmed mindset of always obeying higher authority figures imbued into them by the [[Kaminoan]]s, marking the beginning of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]] and leading on to the rise of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]].

Almost all of the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] were [[Death/Legends|killed]] upon the issuance of Order 66, and most of the survivors were killed in the purge that followed. The Jedi Order survived through the acts of surviving Jedi, such as [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]], passing on the ways of [[The Force/Legends|the Force]] and the Jedi to promising [[Force-sensitive/Legends|Force-sensitives]] such as [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]].

==History==
{{Quote|Statement: Overwhelming odds is also a good tactic, master. There are few Jedi that can long hold their ground against a hundred attackers all firing at once&hellip; or being turned on by their own troops.|[[HK-47]]|<ref name="Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords">''[[Star Wars: Knights of the Old Republic II: The Sith Lords]]''</ref>}}
===Prelude to Order 66===
{{Quote|I sense a plot to destroy the Jedi. The dark side of the Force surrounds the Chancellor.|[[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]]|<ref name="RotS" />}}
Order 66 could be found in the document entitled [[Contingency Orders for the Grand Army of the Republic: Order Initiation, Orders 1 Through 150|''Contingency Orders for the Grand Army of the Republic: Order Initiation, Orders 1 through 150, GAR Document CO(CL) 56-95'']], a document containing a series of special contingency orders that covered any and all emergency situations, which the [[Cloning/Legends|clones]] that comprised the [[Grand Army of the Republic/Legends|Grand Army of the Republic]] (GAR) were prepared to execute, immediately and without question, and only in specific cases of extreme necessity. The order was also programmed into the Clones, through an [[Inhibitor chip/Legends|inhibitor chip]]. The chip was originally designed as a fail-safe by Jedi Master [[Sifo-Dyas/Legends|Sifo-Dyas]] against rogue Jedi.<ref name="Conspiracy">{{TCW|Conspiracy}}</ref> However, when the Sith murdered Sifo-Dyas and hijacked the Clone Army project, they reprogrammed the chip to brainwash the Clones into murdering the Jedi for being perceived traitors to the Republic.

Some of these orders concerned contingencies any armed force could conceivably face. Many dealt with contingencies specifically involving the GAR [[Supreme Commander]]&mdash;in this case, [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]]&mdash;and the effect on the chain of command were he ever to become incapacitated or declared unfit to issue orders. In particular, [[Order 65/Legends|Order 65]] dealt with the detention and possible execution of the Supreme Chancellor by the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Republic]] if he became unfit for office, further hiding the true intention of Order 66. Sufficiently buried among the other one hundred forty-nine orders so as to almost escape notice, Contingency Order 66 specifically dealt with the effect on the chain of command were issues to arise involving the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]]. The text of the order ran:

{{ExcerptIU|'''''Order 66:''' In the event of Jedi officers acting against the interests of the Republic, and after receiving specific orders verified as coming directly from the Supreme Commander (Chancellor), GAR commanders will remove those officers by lethal force, and command of the GAR will revert to the Supreme Commander (Chancellor) until a new command structure is established.''|attrib=Order 66 text<ref name="RCTC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref>}}

Under close examination, the text of Order 66 exposed several distinctions that set it apart from the other contingency orders. First, the majority of the other known contingency orders took into account other sources of command authority&mdash;the [[Vice Chair/Legends|Vice Chair]] [[Mas Amedda/Legends|Mas Amedda]], the [[Senate Security Committee]], the [[Jedi Council/Legends|Jedi Council]], the [[Republic High Command/Legends|GAR High Command]]&mdash;while Order 66 could only be issued by the GAR Supreme Commander&mdash;in this case, Palpatine. Second, it was not required that the Security Council or a Senate majority declare that the Jedi were acting against Republic interests; Palpatine alone had the power to make that determination. Third, GAR commanders were not required to authenticate the order, or even to report it to any other command authority. If the order came directly from Palpatine, using specific command phrasing and over specific communications channels pre-approved by him for this express purpose, the inhibitor chips would immediately brainwash the Clones into obeying the order. Fourth, there was no apparent mechanism for rescinding the order. Once given, it had to be followed. The chips would force the Clones to obey without question, the moment the order was issued.<ref name="RCTC" />

Finally, there was no proviso&mdash;as there was in other known contingency orders&mdash;that the Jedi were to be detained and that lethal force should be used ''if necessary''; the order explicitly specified that they were to be removed by lethal force. Though the true purpose of this specific command was to satisfy Darth Sidious's wish to eliminate the Jedi as a threat to his power, the insistence on lethal force could have been rationalized on general&mdash;that is, non-[[Sith/Legends|Sith]]&mdash;grounds: it could be argued that any attempt to detain a Jedi who did not wish to be detained would fail, except in the event that said Jedi was faced with overwhelming GAR numbers, and even then, such an attempt would likely result in numerous unnecessary GAR casualties. The use of lethal force would therefore be considered necessary to preserve the lives of GAR soldiers and officers.

In order to test out Order 66, [[Order 99]] was programmed into the [[Separatist Droid Army/Legends|Separatist Droid Army]], being issued to [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-Series battle droid]] "[[Coppertop]]" during the [[Battle of Bogoa]].<ref name="The Only Good Clanker">{{TCWComicCite|6.26|The Only Good Clanker}}</ref> To further ensure that various clone troopers carried out the plan when the time came, the order was programmed into a biochip implanted into their brains during development.

[[File:PrematureExecution-TU.png|thumb|left|250px|[[Tiplar/Legends|Tiplar]] was killed when Protocol 66 was prematurely activated within [[Tup/Legends|Tup]].]]
In [[20 BBY/Legends|20 BBY]], however, the Order was nearly prematurely exposed due to a malfunction in [[Tup/Legends|Tup's]] biochip that resulted in his alternating between his regular self and a trance-like state, the latter of which resulted in him betraying and shooting a Jedi Master named [[Tiplar/Legends|Tiplar]] during a battle, and forcing a Republic retreat from the planet.<ref name="The Unknown">{{TCW|The Unknown}}</ref> Darth Sidious, the alter ego of Palpatine, as well as his Sith Apprentice Darth Tyranus, otherwise known as Count Dooku, learned of this from Admiral Trench, and planned to have Tup abducted during transport to Kamino to investigate his erratic behavior, realizing that his current status would most likely result in their true plans for the war, including the contingency order, being exposed to the Jedi. The ARC Trooper [[Fives/Legends|Fives]] alongside [[Rex/Legends|Rex]] managed to retrieve Tup, although this also resulted in the former uncovering the order and thus the conspiracy. Fives was later killed by [[Fox/Legends|Fox]] due to Palpatine deceitfully framing him for an assassination attempt, and unable to tell either Anakin Skywalker or Rex about the contingency order, the overall conspiracy, or the Supreme Chancellor's involvement in it due to being drugged earlier.

In [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], Order 66 was issued by Palpatine toward the end of the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]. The official reason given for its execution was the onset of an [[Showdown on Coruscant|attempted Jedi coup]] against the Republic; in reality, it was the culmination of a [[Grand Plan/Legends|chain of events]] orchestrated by Palpatine over a period of decades, all designed to end the [[Jedi Order/Legends|Jedi Order]] and to bring about the domination of the Sith. Just days earlier, the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] had passed the [[Security Act amendment]], which gave Palpatine authority to disband the Jedi Order.<ref name="ROTS nov">[[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith'' novelization]]</ref>

After the death of [[General/Legends|General]] [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] at the hands of [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Masters]] Mace Windu, [[Kit Fisto/Legends|Kit Fisto]], [[Agen Kolar/Legends|Agen Kolar]], and [[Saesee Tiin/Legends|Saesee Tiin]] stormed the Supreme Chancellor's [[Chancellor's Suite/Legends|office]], intent on arresting Palpatine, who had been revealed to them as the elusive [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Sidious by [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]]. Kolar, Tiin and Fisto were quickly cut down by Sidious, but Windu was able to hold him off and eventually disarm him. Skywalker then arrived to find the Supreme Chancellor, looking defeated, attempting to surrender in exchange for his life. When it became evident that Windu was going to kill Sidious, Skywalker , who needed Sidious alive to save his wife, [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], from the possibility of a presaged demise, betrayed Windu, which gave the Sith Lord the opportunity to destroy the Jedi Master. Windu's "assassination attempt" provided the Chancellor with pretext necessary to enact Order 66.

Anakin Skywalker, for his part, was horror over what he just did. Sidious, now "scarred" from the "attempt on his life," took advantage of Skywalker's emotional distress and pressured him to turn to the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side of the Force]]. Unsure what to do and feeling he could never be forgiven for what he had done, as well as desperate to save Padme, Skywalker betrayed the Jedi and was "knighted" by Sidious as his new apprentice, Darth Vader, Lord of the Sith. Vader would have an important role to play in carrying out his new master's plan.

===Execution of the Order===
{{Quote|It will be done, my Lord.|Commander [[Gree (clone trooper)/Legends|Gree]] complies with Order 66|<ref name="RotS" />}}
At 2100 hours local time, on the one-thousand-eighty-ninth day of the Clone Wars,<ref name="O66" /> Palpatine retired to his private office in the [[Republic Executive Building/Legends|Republic Executive Building]], activated his comm unit and issued Order 66. He employed a channel that made the authenticity of the order unquestionable, but ironically, the signal was encrypted using a [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Separatist]] code&mdash;one of the rare clues that he was, in fact, the hidden hand behind both sides of the war.<ref name="RoF">''[[Reversal of Fortune]]''</ref>

Palpatine sent word via the office of the Chancellor to all of the [[Clone Commander/Legends|clone commanders]] in the army. Upon Palpatine issuing the order, the chips immediately activated and then brainwashed the Clones into believing that the Jedi were traitors to the Republic that needed to be executed. Despite serving and forming relationships with the Jedi for past three years, the activation of their inhibitor chips erased their loyalty and forced them to obey the command without question. On countless planets across the [[Galaxy/Legends|galaxy]], the Jedi were caught off guard by the sudden betrayal of their Clones Troopers and cut down by them. Three years of non-stop galactic warfare polluted the Force with the dark side, clouding Jedi perception even further. Because the clones harbored no malice nor hatred but were merely following an order that they were programmed to obey, they had no ill intent in their heart, which might have given some warning to the Jedi via the Force.<ref name="ROTS nov" />

[[File:Yoda-heartache.png|thumb|right|180px|[[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] feels the [[Disturbance in the Force/Legends|effects]] of Order 66 in the Force.]]
Although it was impossible for Palpatine to have issued the order to every single commander individually, he did take the time to contact several personally before the Order was relayed throughout the army as a whole. Within the first minutes of the Order, several members of the Jedi Council had been killed, including [[Plo Koon/Legends|Plo Koon]] on [[Cato Neimoidia/Legends|Cato Neimoidia]], shot down by [[Clone Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Jai'galaar (clone)|Jag]]; [[Stass Allie/Legends|Stass Allie]] on [[Saleucami/Legends|Saleucami]], at the hands of Commander [[Neyo/Legends|Neyo]] and [[CT-3423]]; [[Aayla Secura/Legends|Aayla Secura]] on [[Felucia/Legends|Felucia]] fell to Commander [[Bly/Legends|Bly]] and members of the [[327th Star Corps/Legends|327th Star Corps]]; and [[Ki-Adi-Mundi/Legends|Ki-Adi-Mundi]] on [[Mygeeto/Legends|Mygeeto]], who managed to deflect a few shots before being overwhelmed by Commander [[Bacara/Legends|Bacara]] and the [[Galactic Marines/Legends|Galactic Marines]]. On [[Utapau/Legends|Utapau]], Obi-Wan Kenobi was riding a [[Varactyl/Legends|varactyl]] named [[Boga/Legends|Boga]] when Commander [[Cody/Legends|Cody]] executed the Order, ordering an [[All Terrain Tactical Enforcer/Legends|AT-TE]] to fire upon him, but Kenobi managed to survive and escape the planet. He soon reunited with [[Grand Master/Legends|Grand Master]] Yoda, who had also escaped a sneak attack by Commander [[Gree (clone trooper)/Legends|Gree]] and a second clone trooper on [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], beheading both clone commander and trooper in the process.

Although Order 66 was only issued to the Grand Army of the Republic, a [[Unidentified IG-100 MagnaGuard (Gold)|MagnaGuard droid]] on Utapau implied upon being reactivated that a similar order to destroy all Jedi was implemented for at least that droid.<ref name="ROTS VG">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode III ''Revenge of the Sith'' video game]]</ref>

Not all clone troopers obeyed the Order, however. On [[Murkhana/Legends|Murkhana]], [[Roan Shryne]] and [[Olee Starstone]] were rescued from Order 66 by members of [[Ion Team]]. Led by [[Climber (clone)|Climber]], they initially questioned the validity of the order, and even upon confirmation, refused to side with the government over those who had fought alongside them, having developed an affinity for the Jedi. [[Omega Squad]], [[Delta Squad/Legends|Delta Squad]], and [[Ordo Skirata]] did not even hesitate to disobey the order, though all of them feigned compliance to avoid suspicion, as they had already formed doubts about Palpatine and his new [[Centax-2/Legends|Centax]] clones. Captain [[Maze (clone trooper)|Maze]], as well, did not execute [[Arligan Zey]]. In all other recorded instances, [[Clone commando/Legends|Commandos]] and [[Advanced Recon Commando/Legends|ARC troopers]] obeyed it.<ref name="Dark Lord">''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

===Raid on the Jedi Temple===
{{Quote|I saw thousands of troops attack the Jedi Temple. That's why I went looking for Yoda.|[[Bail Prestor Organa/Legends|Bail Organa]]|<ref name="RotS" />}}
[[File:ShaKoonOrder66-STD.jpg|thumb|left|220px|In the Jedi Archives, [[Sha Koon]] evades attack by the 501st Legion]]
{{Main|Operation: Knightfall/Legends}}
On [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], [[Senate Emergency Response]] announced a state of martial law over the [[Planet/Legends|planet]], and declared the [[Jedi Temple/Legends|Jedi Temple]] under military lockdown. Order 66 authorized the newly christened Darth Vader and the [[501st Legion/Legends|501st Legion]] to attack the Jedi Temple; however, deciding to take a more surprise-attack approach, a mission named [[Operation: Knightfall/Legends|Operation: Knightfall]] was devised where the 501st attacked any Jedi they found in the Temple&mdash;Masters, [[Padawan/Legends|Padawans]], even [[Jedi Initiate/Legends|younglings]]. They also massacred non-Jedi staff, including administrators, trainers, and guards. No Jedi within the building were spared, but some escaped, including [[Shaak Ti/Legends|Shaak Ti]], [[Sha Koon]], [[Kazdan Paratus]] and [[Jin-Lo Rayce]].

==Aftermath==
{{Quote|Would it have been too much to ask for the order to have come through ''before'' I gave him back the bloody lightsaber?|Commander Cody, speaking of Obi-Wan Kenobi, after receiving Order 66|<ref name="ROTS nov" />}}
Although Order 66 greatly depleted the Jedi Order's ranks, with estimates that less than 100 Jedi surviving it,<ref name="Order 66: Destroy All Jedi">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref> it was only the beginning of the [[Great Jedi Purge/Legends|Great Jedi Purge]], which stretched on for years and claimed the lives of many of the survivors of the initial onslaught. Nearly all the surviving Jedi Knights were hunted down and killed by Darth Vader, while Order 66 remained in effect indefinitely among the ranks of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] newly christened [[Stormtrooper/Legends|stormtroopers]]. Masters Kenobi and Yoda, like many others, chose to go into exile, on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and [[Dagobah/Legends|Dagobah]] respectively. There they eluded Imperial forces for many years, a feat few of their contemporaries could claim.

==Documented victims==
{{Quote|Every single Jedi, including your friend, Obi-Wan Kenobi, is now an enemy of the Republic.|Darth Sidious to Darth Vader|<ref name="RotS" />}}
[[File:Order_66_001.jpg|thumb|right|[[Unidentified Jedi General|A Jedi]] about to be killed during Order 66]]

==Known survivors==
It was said that fewer than one hundred Jedi&mdash;approximately one percent of the entire Order&mdash;survived Order 66.<ref name="Order 66: Destroy All Jedi">{{InsiderCite|87|Order 66: Destroy All Jedi}}</ref> However, the number seemed closer to two hundred.<ref name="DHBoards">{{DHBoards|subdomain=boards|url=viewtopic.php?t=12669&postdays=0&postorder=asc&start=15|thread=DARK TIMES #7: K'Kruhk goes native!|user=[[Randy Stradley]]}}</ref> The anti-Jedi sentiment that Palpatine had fostered during the Clone Wars and the false reports of an attempted Jedi coup had branded the Jedi as warmongering traitors. Hated by the galaxy at large and unable to challenge Palpatine's new government directly, these survivors were forced into hiding. Many of them were hunted down and killed over the next two decades by Vader and his agents.

[[File:Zao_survivor.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Jedi Master [[Zao]] after Order 66]]
Initially, four Jedi on [[Dellalt/Legends|Dellalt]] escaped with their lives: [[Klossi Anno]], [[Deran Nalual]], [[Siadem Forte]], and [[Iwo Kulka]]. A group that was fighting on Murkhana were saved by their troops but one of their number, [[Bol Chatak]], was later killed by Vader.<ref name="Dark Lord" /> The other Jedi, Roan Shryne and Olee Starstone, then fled, meeting up with the group fleeing Dellalt. Forte and Kulka died at Darth Vader's hands, along with Shryne, while the others escaped to attempt to attack the Empire on smaller fronts.<ref name="Dark Lord" /> A group of several Jedi combatants in the [[Battle of Shumari]],<ref name="Perfect Evil">"[[Perfect Evil]]"</ref> except for the young [[Tao (Sith Apprentice)|Tao]], were all hunted down by the Sith. [[Dass Jennir]] led his own fight against the Sith along with a group of rebels, while fellow Jedi [[Kai Hudorra]] and [[Noirah Na]] went into [[Galactic City/Legends|Imperial City]] to try and become "normal" citizens.<ref name="ItU" /> [[Kai Justiss]] attempted to hide from bounty hunters. [[Ekria/Legends|Ekria]], [[Zonder/Legends|Zonder]], and [[Drake Lo'gaan/Legends|Drake Lo'gaan]] escaped Felucia alive, though Zonder died in a duel against Vader.<ref name="RoF" /> [[Chase Piru]] watched after younglings from the Soaring Hawkbat Clan, including [[Seddwia]], [[Jiro (Jedi)|Jiro]], and [[Kennan Taanzer]].<ref name="DT:P">''[[Star Wars: Dark Times: Parallels]]''</ref> [[Tholme/Legends|Tholme]] died at some point and had a funeral pyre on [[Anzat (species)|Anzat]].<ref name="THE">''[[Star Wars: Republic: Hidden Enemy]]''</ref> [[Beyghor Sahdett]] slaughtered the clones that attacked him, and a [[Unidentified Human Jedi (Beyghor Sahdett)|female Jedi]] was able to hide from her clones.<ref name="ItU" />

Obi-Wan Kenobi, Yoda,<ref name="RotS" /> and Shaak Ti were the only High Council members to survive the initial purge.<ref name="TFU">''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]''</ref> [[Maris Brood]] survived and went into hiding along with Shaak Ti on Felucia, while [[Kento Marek]] hid amongst the [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]] on Kashyyyk. [[Aven Rolk]] survived, as he was frozen in stasis for decades in an [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]], and planned to rebuild the Jedi Order but later died in an ice cave on the planet [[Zissh]].

[[Celeste Morne]] escaped the initial order as she had slept in an Oubliette since the [[Mandalorian Wars]]. She later was awakened by Darth Vader on board the smuggling vessel ''[[Uhumele]]''. She survived her confrontation with Vader, but died nearly a hundred years later at the hands of Vader's descendant [[Cade Skywalker]], in an act of mercy, on [[Had Abbadon]].

At a [[Conclave on Kessel|meeting]] on [[Kessel/Legends|Kessel]], the Sith executed [[Koffi Arana]], [[Tsui Choi/Legends|Tsui Choi]], [[Roblio Darté]], [[Jastus Farr]], [[Ma'kis'shaalas/Legends|Ma'kis'shaalas]], [[Shadday Potkin/Legends|Shadday Potkin]], [[Bultar Swan/Legends|Bultar Swan]], and [[Sia-Lan Wezz]]. [[Morvet Storm]] was killed soon after, when Vader attacked his home; however, his [[Havet Storm|son]] escaped Vader.<ref name="Purge">[[Purge (comic book)|''Purge'']]</ref>

[[File:Falon_GreyX2.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Falon Grey]] hid on [[Dantooine/Legends|Dantooine]].]]
[[Aqinos]] and his [[Iron Knight]]s hid on [[Dweem]], while Lady [[Caryn (Jedi)|Caryn]] took a Padawan, [[Ana Tathis]], and then fled into the [[Unknown Regions/Legends|Unknown Regions]]. While Ana Tathis eventually joined the Rebel Alliance, Caryn's final fate remained unknown. [[Minos Fel'Kona]] and his father, [[Jonas Fel'Kona]], fled the devastated [[Cularin system/Legends|Cularin system]] and disappeared. [[Geith Eris]], [[Callista Ming]], and [[Plett]] hid on [[Belsavis/Legends|Belsavis]] away from the fighting though were eventually found. However, Plett escaped and established a sanctuary elsewhere for other surviving Jedi.<ref name="CoJ">[[Children of the Jedi (novel)|''Children of the Jedi'']]</ref> [[Bon (Jedi)|Bon]] and [[Nia]] were found by a traveler and escaped the Purge. [[Darrus Jeht/Legends|Darrus Jeht]] tricked his clone troops and fled to parts unknown. [[Ylenic It'kla]] later died on Alderaan during its destruction,<ref name="RebelDawn">''[[Rebel Dawn]]''</ref> while [[Bardan Jusik]] fled to [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]].<ref name="Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice">''[[Legacy of the Force: Sacrifice]]''</ref> [[Drakka Judarrl]], [[Bre'ano Umakk]] and her [[Drakka Judarrl's Master|master]] hid on Dantooine, [[Matarmeno Krahnn]] was exiled to [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]], [[Antaria Wellos]] remained on [[Rori/Legends|Rori]] well into the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], and Quinlan Vos presumably hid on Kashyyyk with [[Khaleen Hentz/Legends|Khaleen Hentz]] and their son, [[Korto Vos]].<ref name="THE" /> [[Tallisibeth Enwandung-Esterhazy]], [[Arligan Zey]], [[Kina Ha]] and Bardan Jusik survived and were brought to Mandalore by [[Nyreen Vollen]].<ref name="O66" /> Jedi Master [[Hylon]] and his apprentice, [[Dendro]], were cut down by Vader during a [[Battle of Otavon XII|fierce clash]] on Otavon XII.

[[Darrin Arkanian]] was killed by [[High Inquisitor]] [[Antinnis Tremayne]], but his apprentice, [[Corwin Shelvay/Legends|Corwin Shelvay]], escaped. To escape a similar fate, [[Neth Enasteri]] left his family and fled into the [[Outer Rim Territories/Legends|Outer Rim]]. [[Ydra Kilwallen Sibwarra|Ydra Kilwallen]] and her husband lived in peace for several years until they were lost to the [[Ssi-ruu]]. [[Niebur Boton]], [[Dama Montalvo]], a [[Gotal/Legends|Gotal]] Jedi,<ref name="ItU" /> and [[Halagad Ventor]] were tortured by Vader, with Ventor giving the locations of several surviving Jedi, along with his friend [[Ashka Boda]]'s hiding spot. While Boton was tortured to death and mutilated by Vader, Ventor was released and went insane because of the deaths he had caused, though he was eventually redeemed. [[Ameesa Darys]] was killed by [[Arden Lyn]], while the [[Last Curator of Records]], [[Aidan Bok]], [[Axton Tredway]] (though some of Tredway's relatives survived), and [[Unidentified Jedi (Talasea)|another Jedi]] on [[Talasea]] were hunted and killed by the Sith Lord.

[[Kaoln]], [[Gruu Dunrik]], [[Drun Cairnwick/Legends|Drun Cairnwick]], [[Dorn Tavers]], [[Tyneir Renz]], [[Rachi Sitra]], [[Fable Astin/Legends|Fable Astin]], [[Qu Rahn/Legends|Qu Rahn]], [[Echuu Shen-Jon]], [[Rahm Kota/Legends|Rahm Kota]], Corwin Shelvay, Drakka Judarrl, Ana Tathis, and Ylenic It'kla were some of the few remaining Jedi who had joined the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebel Alliance]] and fought with the legendary [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] against the Empire, though Ylenic perished during the destruction of Alderaan, but some of the others who survived the war, such as Corwin, later joined Luke's New Jedi Order. [[Death Star prisoner|A Jedi]] that was captured by the Empire led the [[Death Star Uprising]], during which he was killed.<ref name="BFII">''[[Star Wars: Battlefront II]]''</ref> Fable Astin and [[Fable Astin's mother|her mother]] joined the Alliance and helped combat the Empire. [[Ranik Solusar]] and his [[Kam Solusar|son]] were hunted, with Kam eventually joining the [[New Jedi Order]]. Qu Rahn was eventually slain by an [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Imperial Inquisitor]] shortly after the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]]. However, his spirit transcended the physical plane and would help [[Kyle Katarn]] in his quest for the [[Valley of the Jedi]]. [[Vima-Da-Boda]] hid in shame in the Outer Rim after the Order's fall.<ref name="DE">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire]]''</ref> Echuu Shen-Jon had gone into hiding early into the Clone Wars on [[Krant]], due to the fact he had fallen to the dark side. He later reemerged and saved [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]] from a squad of stormtroopers. He was later struck down by Vader after a fierce duel, but lived on as a Force spirit.<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>

Vima-Da-Boba, [[Empatojayos Brand]],<ref name="DEII">''[[Star Wars: Dark Empire II]]''</ref> [[T'ra Saa/Legends|T'ra Saa]],<ref name="THE" /> [[K'Kruhk]], as well as possible students of his,<ref name="NEC" /> [[Nichos Marr/Legends|Nichos Marr]], Aqinos, and most members of the Iron Knights, and [[Ephaan Kenzon]], including some of his students, later joined Luke Skywalker's New Jedi Order. Brand had been severely injured by Vader during a dogfight near Ganathan Space during the Purge, but was rescued and outfitted with a cybernetic life support suit. He later sacrificed himself to help defeat a reborn Palpatine.

[[Ikrit]] went into a [[Hibernation trance/Legends|hibernation trance]] in 378 BBY on [[Yavin 4/Legends|Yavin 4]], remaining undiscovered during the Purge.<ref name="The Golden Globe">''[[Junior Jedi Knights: The Golden Globe]]''</ref> He joined the New Jedi Order after awaking in [[22 ABY/Legends|22 ABY]],<ref name="Promises">''[[Junior Jedi Knights: Promises]]''</ref> and died four years later during the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]] sacrificing himself to cover the escape of several other Jedi.<ref name="Conquest">''[[The New Jedi Order: Edge of Victory I: Conquest]]''</ref>

[[Beldorion]],<ref name="Planet of Twilight">''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref> [[Jerec (Inquisitor)|Jerec]], [[Danaan Kerr]], [[Maw (Dark Jedi)|Maw]], [[Travgen]], [[Antinnis Tremayne]], [[Dray (Fallen Jedi)|Dray]], [[Quarmall]], [[Sardoth]], [[Jedgar]] and [[Sarcev Quest]] fell to the dark side and were eventually killed by other Jedi or Vader; except Travgen who was eventually redeemed. [[Darth Krayt|A'Sharad Hett]] eventually fell to the dark side too, renamed himself Darth Krayt and created the [[One Sith]]; ironically becoming the main culprit for the [[Third Jedi Purge]].<ref name="NEC" />

Shaak Ti, Rahm Kota, and Kazdan Paratus were all confronted by Darth Vader's secret apprentice, [[Galen Marek]], during the Purge as part of the latter's training. Only Kota survived and apprenticed the young, misled youth to [[Light side of the Force/Legends|the light]], which in turn led to Maris Brood's redemption. Kota went on to join the Rebel Alliance, and led the mission to capture the [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star plans]], despite his blindness. [[Jax Pavan]]<ref name="CNI:JT">''[[Coruscant Nights I: Jedi Twilight]]''</ref> and [[Laranth Tarak]] tried to undo the Empire on Coruscant. K'Kruhk eventually took a [[Chase Piru|Padawan]]<ref name="NEC" /> to the [[Hidden Temple (Arkinnea)|Hidden Temple]].

[[File:Obi-Wan_Kenobi.jpg|thumb|left|200px|Ben Kenobi in exile on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]]]]
[[Fy-Tor-Ana]] and [[Garen Muln]] hid on [[Ilum/Legends|Ilum]] and were eventually killed when they met on the secret [[Jedi asteroid]].<ref name="The Last of the Jedi: Underworld">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Underworld]]''</ref> [[Ry-Gaul]] was undercover during Order 66 but also fled to the Jedi asteroid, where he was killed too.<ref name="The Last of the Jedi: Against the Empire">''[[The Last of the Jedi: Against the Empire]]''</ref> [[Unidentified Human Jedi (Jedi Temple)|A Jedi]] attempted to attack a squad of clones at the Temple and was killed. [[Taj Junak]] sacrificed himself to save his academy and was killed by stormtroopers. [[Nos'lyn]] hid on Tatooine and helped Force-sensitives learn the ways of the Force. [[Qid Proko]] worked as a technician, and [[Urootar]] was killed on Kashyyyk by a bounty hunter.<ref name="ItU" />

Jedi Master Falon Grey hid on Dantooine. During the [[Imperial Era/Legends|Imperial Period]], he led a [[Battle of Dantooine (Imperial Period)|rebellion]] against local Imperial stormtroopers. The elite clone trooper X2, having left Imperial service, helped Grey in the battle, but ultimately, [[X1]] arrived and killed Grey.<ref name="SWBF Elite Squadron" />

Jedi Master [[Iri Camas]] was tracked by the 501st Legion on [[Celen]]. Luring a [[Squad 40|group of four clone commandos]] into the building, he ignited a gas line, causing the building to detonate. While three of the clones escaped, Camas and Bry were killed in the explosion; his lightsaber was later found half-melted in a wall opposite the explosion.

[[Valara Saar]], [[Ood Bnar]],<ref name="DEII" /> [[Ferus Olin]], [[Thracia Cho Leem]], [[Codi Ty]], and Zao<ref name="ItU" /> were not active in the Jedi Order and therefore were not hunted by the Sith. [[Vergere]] was not in the galaxy at the time due to allowing herself to be captured by the [[Yuuzhan Vong|"Far-Outsiders"]] and was thus unaffected.

[[The Dark Woman|An'ya Kuro]], an enigmatic and powerful Jedi Master, perished at Vader's hands in what Palpatine dubbed the final action of the Great Jedi Purge.<ref name="Extinction">{{Tales|issue1=1|issue2=2|Extinction}}</ref> A small group of Jedi Padawans survived the order by stowing away aboard a freighter.<ref name="Salvaged">{{CWACite|9|Salvaged}}</ref>

==Missing in action==
There were many Jedi whose fate after Order 66 remained unknown. In the chaotic early days of the Empire, there were many reasons the fate of certain members of the Order remained unclear, chief among them being that either no body was discovered or the troopers tasked with the execution had been killed. Among the missing were [[Depa Billaba/Legends|Depa Billaba]], who was believed to be recovering from past wounds at the time of the attack on the Jedi Temple, and Master [[Coleman Kcaj/Legends|Coleman Kcaj]], a member of the Jedi Council, who was also believed to have been on Coruscant during Operation: Knightfall. Another missing Master was [[Eeth Koth/Legends|Eeth Koth]], a former Council member. Obi-Wan Kenobi assumed that his longtime friend [[Bant Eerin/Legends|Bant Eerin]] was killed.

==Behind the scenes==
[[File:Quinlanvosdeath.jpg|thumb|right|200px|The apparent death of Vos, excluded from the final version of ''Revenge of the Sith'']]
The first indirect mention of Order 66 was in the [[Star Wars: A New Hope (novelization)|novelization]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''A New Hope'']], ghostwritten by [[Alan Dean Foster]] and published in [[1976]], which stated that the Jedi were "exterminated through treachery and deception."

Originally, Order 66 was to happen in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Star Wars'': Episode II ''Attack of the Clones'']] hence the subtitle to make it more accurate, but was pushed back one film.<ref>{{WebCite|url=http://imaginarycinema.com/sith.html|text=STAR WARS EPISODE III REVENGE OF THE SITH (2005)|work=[http://imaginarycinema.com Imaginary Cinema]|archivedate=20160520012229}}</ref>

In the first draft of [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith]] ([[April 13]], [[2003]]), the number of Jedi who were killed was "more extensive."<ref name="TMOSWROTS">''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''</ref> The following excerpt from this draft is taken from the book ''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]'':

''On Mygeeto, clones blast KI-ADI-MUNDI and SAESEE TIIN. On Saleucami, they kill KIT FISTO, BARRISS OFFEE, and ADI GALLIA. On Kashyyyk, MINA PODIA is gunned down&mdash;but YODA saves himself. On Cato Neimoidia, PLO KOON is blasted out of the sky, while an unnamed Jedi lies dead on the planet surface. On Felucia, AAYLA SECURA and QUINLAN VOS are silenced forever.''<ref name="TMOSWROTS" />

The [[Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith (novelization)|novelization]] of ''Revenge of the Sith'' says, "The clones have no malice, no hatred, not the slightest ill intent that might give warning. They are only following orders",<ref name="ROTS nov" /> but the [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|junior novelization]] says, "Yoda could sense the faint aura of the dark side clinging to them."<ref name="ROTS jnov">[[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith (junior novelization)|''Star Wars: Revenge of the Sith'' junior novelization]]</ref>

[[Pablo Hidalgo]] stated that "Order 66 is not some pre-programmed genetic trigger. It's not some Manchurian Candidate brainwash button. It's rather just one of a catalogue of orders that clone commanders and their soldiers are trained since birth to follow without question."<ref name="Hidalgo">{{InsiderCite|83|Star Wars Q&A|Ask the Master}}</ref> 

The order preceding Order 66 is [[Order 65/Legends|Order 65]], which stated that the Supreme Chancellor would be removed from office by the GAR if the Galactic Senate declared him unfit for duty.<ref name="TC">''[[Republic Commando: True Colors]]''</ref>

In the ''[[Star Wars: The Complete Saga]]'' Blu-ray set, the special-features disc shows the animation test for Order 66. It has more Jedi killed and different deaths for some. For example, Ki-Adi-Mundi is on a tower. An elevator then reaches the top with a large group of clone troopers inside, who kill him. Another example is Aayla Secura's death on Felucia with a large group of clones. They all kneel as droids pass ahead. Secura asks if they are droids. Bly simply says "no," and kills her. Another deleted scene from the film is set during ''Operation: Knightfall''; Shaak Ti is shown meditating, and asks "What is it, Skywalker?" when Skywalker enters the room. Skywalker does not answer and simply stabs the Jedi Master.

[[Karen Traviss]]'s [[Republic Commando]] novels mentioned that the Contingency Orders were taught and not programmed, resulting in several clones ignoring the order and/or refusing to go through with it outright, even "normal" (that is, a non-Commando, ARC, or any other special-forces clone) clones such as [[Corr Skirata|RC-5108/8843]] "Corr." The novel ''[[Dark Lord: The Rise of Darth Vader]]'' also supports this, as [[Ion Team]] refused to execute the Order, and went rogue. However, the [[The Clone Wars: The Lost Missions|sixth season]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' revealed that the Contingency Orders are indeed planted in the minds of all clone troopers during their development via an organic biochip that subconsciously activates the Orders when given.<ref name="Conspiracy /> <ref name="Fugitive">{{TCW|Fugitive}}</ref><ref name="Orders">{{TCW|Orders (episode)}}</ref>
